text: Only one of the three storage modes from Lesson 71 actually needs anything at all covered in this chapter. Here's exactly which one that is, and the real reason why the other two simply don't apply.

Import mode copies the source data directly into the semantic model, so that copy inevitably goes stale the moment the actual source changes underneath it. DirectQuery, Direct Lake, and live connection modes never copy anything in at all — every single query goes straight to the source live, so there's genuinely nothing left to catch up on. Push mode is different again: an external process pushes new data in directly, with no defined data source of its own.

You can trigger a refresh either on a schedule, which Lesson 77 covers in full, or immediately, right now, on demand. Refresh now doesn't count against your daily scheduled-refresh quota at all — though it still consumes real capacity resources behind the scenes, so it isn't truly unlimited either.

That daily quota depends entirely on where the semantic model actually lives. Shared capacity on Power BI Pro allows up to eight scheduled refreshes a day. Premium Per User, Premium, or Fabric capacity allows up to forty-eight a day instead — and that quota resets daily at exactly twelve oh one AM, in whichever time zone the semantic model's own settings specify.

One detail worth remembering: a data refresh only ever re-imports rows, never the underlying structure. Rename or remove a column at the source without republishing first, and the service's very next refresh fails outright, because it's still expecting the old structure to be there. Lesson 76 covers the gateway that makes on-premises refresh possible at all in the first place.
